events.title: The election of Pope Eugene IV
events.shortBlurb: A Venetian nephew of Gregory XII was chosen pope in the first conclave after the Great Schism, and his stormy reign saw union proclaimed with the Greeks…
body: Martin V died on 20 February 1431, and in the first conclave held since the healing of the Great Schism the cardinals chose, on 3 March 1431 — or on the fourth, as some older authorities reckon — Gabriele Condulmer of Venice, a nephew of Gregory XII made cardinal in 1408. Crowned on 11 March, he took the name Eugene IV.

His long pontificate was a running battle with the conciliar movement: he dissolved the Council of Basel at its opening in 1431, was driven from Rome into exile at Florence in 1434, and fought for years to recover his city. Yet it was Eugene who presided over the Council of Ferrara and Florence, where on 6 July 1439 the decree Laetentur Caeli proclaimed union with the Greeks.

In Florence he also consecrated, on 25 March 1436, the cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore beneath Brunelleschi's new dome. Restored to Rome in 1443, he died there on 23 February 1447, having held the papacy through some of its most turbulent years.
